docs.title: Welcome to Rinku
docs.text:
Rinku is a lightweight Kotlin Multiplatform library designed to simplify deep link handling across iOS, Android, JVM desktop (macOS, Windows, and Linux), and Web (Kotlin/JS and Kotlin/Wasm browsers). By abstracting platform-specific details, Rinku enables developers to manage deep links in a unified manner, enhancing code reuse and maintaining consistency across platforms.

Coding agents can use llms.txt for a concise overview and links to the Markdown documentation.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
This guide presupposes the prior configuration of deeplinks within the native platforms:

  • Android deeplink
  • iOS URL scheme
  • iOS universal link
  • Desktop URL schemes and single-instance setup
  • Web browser history and SPA hosting

docs.title: Installation Process
docs.text:
The library is available via Maven Central 

implementation("dev.theolm:rinku:<latest_version>")
implementation("dev.theolm:rinku-compose-ext:<latest_version>")

docs.title: Gradle Configuration
docs.text:
Both Rinku modules support iosArm64 (physical devices) and iosSimulatorArm64 (Apple Silicon simulators). The iosX64 target (Intel Mac simulators) is no longer supported.

In your build.gradle.kts file you need to: - Include Rinku in commonMain as an api (this is required to export it to iOS) - If you are using Compose multiplatform, also include the compose-extensions - Export the lib in the ios framework

Example: 

kotlin {
    ...
    listOf(
        iosArm64(),
        iosSimulatorArm64()
        // Specify iOS targets
    ).forEach { iosTarget ->
        iosTarget.binaries.framework {
            // Export of Rinku library to the iOS framework
            export("dev.theolm:rinku:<latest_version>")
            ...
        }
    }
    ...
    sourceSets {
        commonMain.dependencies {
            api("dev.theolm:rinku:<latest_version>")

            // For compose multiplatform projects
            implementation("dev.theolm:rinku-compose-ext:<latest_version>")
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Android setup
docs.text: The library provides two types of initialization (KMP only and Compose). Use the one that fits your needs.

docs.title: KMP only
docs.text:
On the Android app, inside the onCreate, call the extension RinkuInit().

class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        RinkuInit()
        setContent {
            App()
        }
    }
}

docs.title: With Compose multiplatform
docs.text:
First, make sure you included rinku-compose-ext in your commonMain dependencies. In the Android app, inside setContent, use the ComponentActivity.Rinku extension to wrap the root of your app.

class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)

        setContent {
            Rinku {
                App()
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: iOS setup
docs.text:
For the iOS platform, deep links are processed within the AppDelegate or SceneDelegate, contingent on the project’s configuration. The primary objective is to intercept the platform-specific deep link and relay it as an argument to Rinku’s handleDeepLink(url) method.

Example within AppDelegate:

@UIApplicationMain
class AppDelegate: NSObject, UIApplicationDelegate {
    ...
    // Provide deepLinkFilter and deepLinkMapper if needed
    let rinku = RinkuIos.init(deepLinkFilter: nil, deepLinkMapper: nil)
    func application(_ app: UIApplication, open url: URL, options: [UIApplication.OpenURLOptionsKey : Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
        rinku.onDeepLinkReceived(url: url.absoluteString)
        return true
    }

    func application(_ application: UIApplication, continue userActivity: NSUserActivity, restorationHandler: @escaping ([UIUserActivityRestoring]?) -> Void) -> Bool {
        if userActivity.activityType == NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb, let url = userActivity.webpageURL {
            let urlString = url.absoluteString
            rinku.onDeepLinkReceived(userActivity: userActivity)
        }
        return true
    }
    ...
}

docs.title: Web setup
docs.text: Use RinkuWeb.start() in your browser entry point or the Web Compose Rinku { App() } wrapper. Both JS and Wasm receive the initial URL and browser Back/Forward through the same common listeners. See the Web guide for lifecycle, history ownership, filters, mappers, samples, and hosting configuration.

docs.title: Common setup
docs.text: In common code, listen for deep links and handle them as your application requires. Android, iOS, desktop, and Web all deliver the same DeepLink model through these listeners.

docs.title: Using Compose
docs.text:
Example RootApp in commonMain:

@Composable
fun RootApp() {
    var deepLink by remember { mutableStateOf<DeepLink?>(null) }
    DeepLinkListener { deepLink = it }
    MainScreen(deepLink)
}

docs.title: KMP only
docs.text:
Just use the suspend function listenForDeepLinks and react as you will.

Example inside a Decompose component (navigation model, interface members, and the application-specific toScreenStack() extension are omitted). Create a coroutine scope for the component and cancel it when the component is destroyed:

import com.arkivanov.essenty.lifecycle.doOnDestroy
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.SupervisorJob
import kotlinx.coroutines.cancel
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class AppComponentImpl(
    private val initialStack: List<Config> = emptyList(),
    componentContext: ComponentContext,
) : AppComponent, ComponentContext by componentContext {
    private val navigation = StackNavigation<Config>()
    private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate)

    init {
        lifecycle.doOnDestroy { scope.cancel() }
        scope.launch { initDeepLinkListener() }
    }

    private suspend fun initDeepLinkListener() {
        listenForDeepLinks {
            navigation.replaceAll(
                *it.toScreenStack().toTypedArray()
            )
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Firing Internal Deeplink
docs.text: Rinku simplifies the process of triggering internal deep links directly from your common Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) code. This feature allows you to easily navigate within your application using a unified approach across all platforms.

docs.title: Triggering a Deep Link
docs.text:
To invoke an internal deep link within your application, pass its URL to Rinku.handleDeepLink. By default, internal calls bypass the configured filter and mapper.

Rinku.handleDeepLink("https://test.deeplink/path?query=true")

In this example, https://test.deeplink/path?query=true represents the URL of the deep link. The URL scheme, path, and query parameters should be replaced with values that are relevant to your application’s routing structure.

docs.title: Applying a filter or mapper
docs.text:
To apply the filter and mapper registered during platform initialization, enable the corresponding flags explicitly:

Rinku.handleDeepLink(
    url = "https://test.deeplink/path?query=true",
    applyFilter = true,
    applyMapper = true,
)

The filter runs before the mapper. Each flag defaults to false and can be enabled independently. Enabling a flag without configuring the corresponding DeepLinkFilter or DeepLinkMapper throws IllegalStateException when that step is reached. See filters and mappers for configuration examples.

By leveraging Rinku’s handleDeepLink method, you can enhance your application’s navigation capabilities, making it easier to programmatically direct users to specific areas of your app from shared KMP code.

docs.title: Type-safe parameters
docs.text: Rinku supports reading and creating type-safe parameters using kotlinx.serialization. Configure the serialization compiler plugin and JSON dependency in your app/module before using the following functions.

docs.title: Getting parameters
docs.text:
Use the DeepLink.getParameter extension with the query parameter name and the KSerializer of the corresponding Kotlin class. A missing parameter throws IllegalArgumentException; an invalid value throws a deserialization exception.

Example:

import dev.theolm.rinku.DeepLink
import dev.theolm.rinku.getParameter
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

@Serializable
data class Name(val name: String)

fun example() {
    val url = "https://example.com/dev/path?test=%7B%22name%22%3A%22Theo%22%7D"
    val deepLink = DeepLink(url)

    val param: Name = deepLink.getParameter(name = "test", kSerializer = Name.serializer())
}

The query value is the percent-encoded JSON {"name":"Theo"}. Rinku decodes the query parameter before deserializing it.

docs.title: Build a URL using Serializable classes
docs.text:
Rinku also provides the Rinku.buildUrl helper to build internal deep links with serializable parameters. Build the URL, then pass it to Rinku.handleDeepLink.

Example:

import dev.theolm.rinku.Rinku
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkParam
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

@Serializable
data class Name(val name: String)

fun example() {
    val testModel = Name("Testing")
    val testParam = DeepLinkParam(
        "testParam",
        testModel,
        Name.serializer()
    )
    val url = Rinku.buildUrl("https://example.com/dev/path", testParam)
    Rinku.handleDeepLink(url)
}

buildUrl appends serialized JSON without percent-encoding it. This example is for internal dispatch; percent-encode query values before sending the URL through a browser or operating-system URL handler. Use a base URL without an existing query or fragment.

docs.title: Deep Link Filters and Mappers
docs.text:
Rinku can reject unwanted external deep links after the platform delivers them to your application. Implement DeepLinkFilter and pass it to the platform initializer. A URL is processed only when isValid returns true.

The filter does not replace URL scheme registration, Android intent filters, or iOS URL scheme and Universal Link configuration. Those settings determine whether the OS delivers the URL to your app. A Rinku filter only controls subsequent processing; it does not authenticate the sender or replace authorization checks.

import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkFilter

object ExampleFilter : DeepLinkFilter {
    override fun isValid(url: String): Boolean =
        url == "rinku://dev.theolm/screenC/"
}

This example deliberately accepts one exact URL. Adapt validation to your supported schemes, hosts, paths, and parameters.

docs.title: Deep link mapper
docs.text:
A DeepLinkMapper transforms an accepted external URL into the internal URL your navigation expects. For example:

  • Android and iOS marketing links can map to one shared internal route.
  • A link to screen C can expand into the full navigation stack A → B → C.
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkMapper

object ExampleMapper : DeepLinkMapper {
    override fun map(url: String): String {
        return if (url == "rinku://dev.theolm/screenC/") {
            "rinku://dev.theolm/screenA/screenB/screenC/"
        } else {
            url
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
On Android, pass the objects to RinkuInit inside ComponentActivity.onCreate:

RinkuInit(
    deepLinkFilter = ExampleFilter,
    deepLinkMapper = ExampleMapper,
)

Alternatively, use the Compose wrapper inside the activity’s setContent:

Rinku(deepLinkFilter = ExampleFilter, deepLinkMapper = ExampleMapper) {
    App()
}

Use only one initialization approach. RinkuIos, RinkuDesktop, and RinkuWeb also accept deepLinkFilter and deepLinkMapper; see the setup, desktop, and Web guides.

External links are filtered before mapping, so validate the original external URL. Internal calls to Rinku.handleDeepLink(url) bypass both steps unless you explicitly enable applyFilter and/or applyMapper; see internal deep links.

docs.title: Demonstrative Samples
docs.text:
The library includes two illustrative examples utilizing the foremost multiplatform navigation libraries: Voyager and Decompose

  • Voyager sample
  • Decompose sample

Note: Only the Voyager sample includes an iOS application (at samples/voyager/iosApp). Nonetheless, the setup for Decompose would mirror that of Voyager.

Note 2: Both examples are using Compose multiplatform.

docs.title: Desktop support
docs.text: Rinku supports JVM 17+ applications on macOS, Windows, and Linux, with or without Compose Desktop. The platform adapter receives URLs, applies your filter and mapper, and delivers DeepLink objects through the same DeepLinkListener / listenForDeepLinks APIs used on mobile. Navigation stays in your application. The existing jvm() target is used; Kotlin/Native desktop targets are not included.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
Add dev.theolm:rinku:<latest_version> to commonMain (or your JVM application). Add dev.theolm:rinku-compose-ext:<latest_version> if using Compose. No separate desktop artifact is needed.

Initialize once, before creating any windows, not inside a composable:

import androidx.compose.ui.window.Window
import androidx.compose.ui.window.application
import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuDesktop

fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    RinkuDesktop(
        applicationId = "com.example.myapp",
        schemes = setOf("myapp"),
        // deepLinkFilter = MyFilter(),
        // deepLinkMapper = MyMapper(),
        onError = { error -> error.printStackTrace() },
    ).use { rinku ->
        if (rinku.start(args) == RinkuDesktop.StartResult.FORWARDED) return
        application(exitProcessOnExit = false) {
            Window(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "My app") {
                App() // Keep DeepLinkListener in your shared UI.
            }
        }
    }
}

For non-Compose applications, keep the adapter alive until your event loop ends, call close() on shutdown, and collect listenForDeepLinks in an application-owned coroutine scope. Rinku includes kotlinx-coroutines-swing on JVM so existing Rinku.handleDeepLink calls have a Main dispatcher even without Compose. Desktop URLs are queued synchronously; listeners execute in the collector’s coroutine context. Install your listener on the appropriate UI dispatcher before navigating.

start() returns PRIMARY for the process that should create the UI, or FORWARDED after a secondary process contacts the primary. Rinku never calls exitProcess. Startup/IPC failures throw; do not respond to them by opening an independent second instance. Repeated start() calls on the same adapter return its original result without reprocessing arguments. A closed adapter cannot restart.

Only absolute, syntactically valid URIs matching the configured schemes are accepted. Pass each URL as a separate argument, without an extra --url= prefix. Percent-encode spaces and JSON values. Other arguments and unsupported schemes are ignored. The filter runs before the mapper; both run on the receiving thread and should be fast and thread-safe. onDeepLinkReceived(url) is also available for applications integrating their own native events. Do not install a competing AWT OpenURI handler when using Rinku’s automatic handler.

docs.title: Startup delivery and limits
docs.text:
• Desktop links wait in an in-memory FIFO until a shared listener is installed. Repeated identical links remain separate events. Use one logical listener: delivery is single-consumer, not broadcast.
  • Up to 64 pending desktop links are retained. When full, the newest link is rejected and onError is called. Events are not persisted across process exits.
  • Each input URL is limited to 16,384 UTF-16 code units; longer inputs are ignored. At most 64 accepted URLs may be supplied in one startup/IPC request.
  • Existing mobile/internal handleDeepLink calls retain their single-pending-value behavior; they are not converted to FIFO delivery. If mixed with desktop links, that pending value is consumed first.
  • onError reports mapping, parsing, queue overflow, and incoming IPC errors. Keep the callback non-throwing. IPC acknowledgement confirms processing by the adapter, not successful navigation or persistence; filtered/invalid links are not navigated. A lost acknowledgement raises an error rather than automatically resending a potentially delivered link.

docs.title: Single-instance behavior
docs.text:
Use a stable, unique applicationId (different IDs for different apps or intentionally separate development/release instances). Instance election uses an OS file lock. Authenticated loopback IPC forwards secondary startup URLs to the primary, including when no UI listener exists yet.

Per-user endpoint data is stored under ~/.rinku/<SHA-256-of-applicationId>/instance (with a separate instance.lock for election), with owner-only POSIX permissions or Windows ACLs. A fresh random token is generated for each primary. The state directory must be on a local filesystem supporting locks and permissions; sandboxed deployments must allow that directory and loopback sockets. Startup discovery retries for approximately five seconds; socket operations have 1.5-second timeouts. The transport is not intended as a security boundary against other code running as the same OS user.

close() releases sockets, the file lock and the native URL handler. OS process termination also releases locks; stale endpoint data is replaced by the next primary. Do not delete the lock file while an instance is running. Single-instance delivery does not automatically focus or restore your application window.

docs.title: Registering a URL scheme
docs.text: As on mobile, registration is the responsibility of the application package/installer, not Rinku. This release covers custom schemes, not verified HTTPS app/universal links. Validate incoming paths and parameters as untrusted input; registering a scheme does not authenticate the sender.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
Rinku installs Desktop.setOpenURIHandler when APP_OPEN_URI is supported. macOS delivers opening events to the packaged application, including startup events. Declare the scheme in your bundle’s Info.plist; with Compose Desktop:

compose.desktop.application.nativeDistributions.macOS {
    bundleID = "com.example.myapp"
    infoPlist {
        extraKeysRawXml = """
            <key>CFBundleURLTypes</key>
            <array><dict>
                <key>CFBundleTypeRole</key><string>Editor</string>
                <key>CFBundleURLName</key><string>com.example.myapp</string>
                <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key><array><string>myapp</string></array>
            </dict></array>
        """.trimIndent()
    }
}

Install/launch the packaged .app so Launch Services recognizes it. Test with open 'myapp://example/second/third' both before and after launching the app. Running with Gradle does not register a protocol or prove native startup behavior. Where AWT OpenURI is unavailable, the application must supply arguments or forward its own native events to onDeepLinkReceived.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Register a per-user protocol in your installer. Example .reg content (replace the executable path):

Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\myapp]
@="URL:My App Protocol"
"URL Protocol"=""

[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\myapp\shell\open\command]
@="\"C:\\Users\\User\\AppData\\Local\\MyApp\\MyApp.exe\" \"%1\""

Quote both executable and URL. The packaged launcher must pass the URL unchanged to main(args). Compose’s MSI packaging alone does not register this scheme; add registration/unregistration to your installer. Test from PowerShell with Start-Process 'myapp://example/second/third'.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
Install a desktop entry under ~/.local/share/applications/myapp.desktop, with an absolute launcher path:

[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=My App
Exec=/opt/myapp/bin/MyApp %u
Terminal=false
MimeType=x-scheme-handler/myapp;

Use a quoted executable path if it contains spaces. Register it using:

update-desktop-database ~/.local/share/applications
xdg-mime default myapp.desktop x-scheme-handler/myapp
xdg-open 'myapp://example/second/third'

Keep %u as a launcher argument; do not interpolate URLs into shell commands. Your installer must also remove associations appropriately on uninstall. Compose’s DEB alone does not provide this setup.

docs.title: Samples and verification
docs.text:
./gradlew :samples:voyager:desktopApp:run --args='rinku-voyager://example/second/third'
./gradlew :samples:decompose:desktopApp:run --args='rinku-decompose://example/second/third'

Both launchers reuse the existing shared navigation and screens. Run a sample a second time with another URL: it should forward the link and exit without opening a second window. macOS bundle scheme declarations are included; Windows/Linux registration remains an installer step as above. Use :samples:voyager:desktopApp:packageDistributionForCurrentOS (or the Decompose equivalent) to build a package on its target OS. Runtime modules include instrumentation/management modules used by the samples’ shared dependencies.

Before shipping, test each packaged application on its OS:

  1. Open a registered link while the app is closed, then while it is already open.
  2. Open repeated links and bursts before the first UI listener is ready.
  3. Verify filters, mappers, encoded parameters, unsupported schemes and invalid URLs.
  4. Start competing processes, terminate the primary abruptly, and reopen a link.
  5. Confirm that a secondary exits, and registration is removed correctly on uninstall.

The desktop CI matrix runs shared/JVM tests, actual child-process IPC/lock-recovery tests and sample compilation on all three operating systems. Native protocol registration and packaged OS-event delivery still require the manual checks above.

docs.title: Web (Kotlin/JS and Kotlin/Wasm)
docs.text: Both rinku-core and rinku-compose-ext support js { browser() } and wasmJs { browser() }. Use the same Maven coordinates and shared DeepLink, filters, mappers, and listeners as on Android, iOS, and desktop. Rinku is a deep-link receiver, not a Web router.

docs.title: Browser contract
docs.text:
RinkuWeb receives:

  • The full current window.location.href at startup, including the site root, unless captureInitialUrl = false.
  • The current full URL on each popstate event, such as browser Back and Forward.

Rinku does not write browser history, intercept pushState or replaceState, observe hashchange, or convert a fragment into a route. Path routing is supported; hash routing is outside this adapter’s contract. A fragment in a received URL is preserved in DeepLink.data, not interpreted as path segments.

Filters run before mappers, once per browser event. The mapper’s output goes through the existing common parser and bounded FIFO queue. Up to 64 platform links can wait for a listener; overflow rejects the newest link and calls onError. Distinct browser events with identical URLs are not deduplicated.

docs.title: Manual initialization
docs.text:
In your Web entry point, start the adapter before creating the UI:

import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuWeb

val rinku = RinkuWeb(
    captureInitialUrl = true,
    deepLinkFilter = myFilter, // optional
    deepLinkMapper = myMapper, // optional
    onError = { error -> println("Deep-link error: $error") },
)
rinku.start()
// Create your UI. Call rinku.close() when disposing the application.

Use only one active adapter per page. Repeated start() calls do nothing; they do not replay the initial URL. close() is idempotent, removes the browser listener, and leaves already queued links available to shared listeners. A closed adapter cannot restart; create a new one instead. Starting another adapter while one is active throws.

Filter/mapper, parsing, and overflow failures go to onError. Initialization/ownership errors throw to the caller. Error callbacks should not throw. The default callback prints the exception. Filters and mappers supplied at startup are also registered for explicit Rinku.handleDeepLink(..., applyFilter = true, applyMapper = true) calls, as on desktop.

docs.title: Compose initialization
docs.text:
Instead of initializing manually, wrap the root of your Web composition:

import dev.theolm.rinku.compose.ext.Rinku

Rinku(
    captureInitialUrl = true,
    deepLinkFilter = myFilter,
    deepLinkMapper = myMapper,
) {
    App()
}

The wrapper uses DisposableEffect to start/close its adapter. Ordinary recomposition does not reinstall it or replay startup. Changing capture/filter/mapper configuration replaces the adapter, capturing the initial URL again if enabled. Remember filter/mapper objects rather than constructing new instances on every recomposition. Updating onError alone does not restart the adapter.

Do not combine the wrapper with a manually started adapter.

docs.title: Shared navigation remains unchanged
docs.text:
Use one logical listener, either the suspending common API:

listenForDeepLinks { deepLink ->
    // Application-specific parsing/navigation, just as on the other platforms.
}

or the existing Compose listener inside App():

DeepLinkListener { deepLink ->
    // Update Voyager, Decompose, or your own navigation.
}

Events are consumed once, not broadcast. Initial URLs received before the listener starts remain queued. The adapter never depends on a navigation library.

docs.title: Application-owned navigation and history
docs.text:
pushState and replaceState do not emit popstate. When navigating internally, the application must update its router itself, or explicitly notify Rinku once:

window.history.pushState(null, "", "/second/third?source=web")
Rinku.handleDeepLink(window.location.href, applyFilter = true, applyMapper = true)

Enable the flags only if you configured the respective filter/mapper. Do not both navigate directly and dispatch the same link if that would duplicate the transition. Do not write a new history entry from a Back/Forward callback: doing so creates a navigation loop. Do not install a second browser-to-router integration for the same events without coordinating it.

docs.title: Hosting and deployment prefixes
docs.text:
Rinku preserves the URL, including deployment prefixes. For https://example.com/app/second?source=web, the shared path contains app and second. If navigation should see only second, remove the prefix in your DeepLinkMapper, preserving the origin, encoded path, query, and fragment. There is no adapter-level basePath setting.

The host must serve your SPA entry point for application routes such as /second/third, including direct requests and reloads. Static resources must still resolve from the deployment root. For example, configure an SPA rewrite/fallback on your host, and use <base href="/app/"> when deploying under /app/. Rinku cannot fix server-side 404s.

docs.title: Samples
docs.text:
Both navigation samples include a webApp module. Run one command at a time:

./gradlew :samples:voyager:webApp:jsBrowserDevelopmentRun
./gradlew :samples:voyager:webApp:wasmJsBrowserDevelopmentRun
./gradlew :samples:decompose:webApp:jsBrowserDevelopmentRun
./gradlew :samples:decompose:webApp:wasmJsBrowserDevelopmentRun

Each sample has application-owned history controls. Open /second/third?source=web directly, navigate with the toolbar, then try browser Back, Forward, and reload. The development servers include an SPA fallback. Existing in-screen back controls operate on the navigation library’s stack; the toolbar’s browser controls operate on browser history.

For a prefixed deployment, change both <base href> and the rinku-base-path meta tag in the sample’s src/webMain/resources/index.html to the same slash-terminated prefix, such as /app/. The sample mapper removes that prefix before shared navigation. Its filter accepts same-origin URLs.

Build distributable bundles with jsBrowserDistribution or wasmJsBrowserDistribution on either webApp module. Wasm requires a browser with Wasm GC support; Kotlin/JS is a separate build, not an automatic runtime fallback.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Install Chrome/Chromium and set CHROME_BIN if it is not discoverable. Run:

./gradlew :rinku-core:jsBrowserTest :rinku-core:wasmJsBrowserTest \
  :rinku-compose-ext:jsBrowserTest :rinku-compose-ext:wasmJsBrowserTest

The suites run shared tests plus real browser-history tests and Compose runtime lifecycle tests. CI also bundles both samples in JS and Wasm. Linking Compose Web builds can require more than the project’s default 2 GB compiler heap; CI uses --max-workers=1 -Pkotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx4g to serialize compilation with a larger heap. Use those options locally when linking the samples or Compose tests if needed. Yarn lockfiles are tracked; after intentionally changing npm dependencies, regenerate them with ./gradlew kotlinUpgradeYarnLock kotlinWasmUpgradeYarnLock.

docs.title: Public API reference
docs.text:
This reference describes the source on main, which may include unreleased changes. Check the documentation and sources at the tag matching your Maven dependency before using a newly added API or platform. Install dev.theolm:rinku:<version> and, for Compose, dev.theolm:rinku-compose-ext:<version> at the same version.

Signatures below omit implementation details. See verified examples for executable code and the setup guide for Gradle and platform registration.

docs.title: Shared model
docs.text:
Import dev.theolm.rinku.DeepLink.

data class DeepLink(
    val data: String,
    val timestamp: Long = Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds(),
)

Clock is kotlin.time.Clock. Construction parses the URL immediately using Ktor; malformed input can throw. The timestamp is creation time in Unix epoch milliseconds, not the time the OS received the link. The original string remains in data.

Read-only properties:

  • schema: String: protocol name. The API spelling is schema, not scheme.
  • host: String: parsed host.
  • encodedPath: String: percent-encoded path.
  • pathSegments: List<String>: decoded path segments, excluding blank segments.
  • encodedQuery: String: encoded query, without the leading ?.
  • queryParameterNames: Set<String>: query keys.
  • parameters: Map<String, String>: decoded query values. Repeated keys collapse to one map entry; the last flattened value wins.

The fragment is retained in data, but has no dedicated public property and is not interpreted as a route. Parsing is not validation or authorization of a route.

docs.title: Dispatch and listening
docs.text:
import dev.theolm.rinku.Rinku
import dev.theolm.rinku.listenForDeepLinks

object Rinku {
    fun handleDeepLink(url: String): Unit
    fun handleDeepLink(
        url: String,
        applyFilter: Boolean = false,
        applyMapper: Boolean = false,
    ): Unit
}

suspend fun listenForDeepLinks(listener: (DeepLink) -> Unit): Unit

These are existing library declarations, not functions to declare in your app.

  • Internal dispatch bypasses filters and mappers unless their flags are enabled.
  • Filtering happens before mapping. Rejection returns without dispatching.
  • An enabled but unconfigured filter/mapper throws IllegalStateException when that step is reached. Filter and mapper exceptions propagate to the caller.
  • Parsing and emission run asynchronously on Dispatchers.Main. A successful return is not confirmation of parsing or navigation; asynchronous failures are not caught by a try/catch around handleDeepLink.
  • Mobile/internal dispatch keeps one pending value, not a FIFO. Rapid dispatches can overwrite an unconsumed value. Desktop/Web adapter events instead use a shared FIFO of up to 64 pending platform links; overflow rejects the newest event.
  • Use one logical listener. Links are consumed once, not broadcast. A pending mobile/internal value is consumed before queued platform links.
  • listenForDeepLinks stays suspended while collecting. Own its coroutine scope and cancel it with the UI/application lifecycle. Callbacks run in the collector’s context; exceptions escape collection. Dispatch to your UI thread as needed.

For Compose, import dev.theolm.rinku.compose.ext.DeepLinkListener:

@Composable
fun DeepLinkListener(listener: (DeepLink) -> Unit)

This starts collection with LaunchedEffect(Unit), cancels when it leaves composition, and uses the latest callback without restarting collection on ordinary recomposition. It does not initialize a platform adapter or navigate automatically.

docs.title: Filters and mappers
docs.text:
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkFilter
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkMapper

interface DeepLinkFilter {
    fun isValid(url: String): Boolean
}

interface DeepLinkMapper {
    fun map(url: String): String
}

Supply these during platform initialization. Filters see the original external URL; mappers return the URL passed to the shared parser. They do not register URL schemes or authenticate senders. See filters and mappers.

docs.title: Serializable query parameters
docs.text:
import dev.theolm.rinku.getParameter
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkParam
import kotlinx.serialization.KSerializer

fun <T> DeepLink.getParameter(name: String, kSerializer: KSerializer<T>): T

class DeepLinkParam<T>(val name: String, value: T, kSerializer: KSerializer<T>) {
    fun serialize(): String
}

// Additional members of the existing Rinku object:
object Rinku {
    fun buildUrl(url: String, vararg parameters: DeepLinkParam<*>): String
    fun buildUrl(
        schema: String,
        host: String,
        path: String? = null,
        vararg parameters: DeepLinkParam<*>,
    ): String
}

Configure the kotlinx.serialization plugin and JSON dependency in your module. getParameter uses the default Json configuration, throws IllegalArgumentException for a missing key, and throws a deserialization exception for an incompatible value. There is no nullable lookup overload or configurable Json instance.

DeepLinkParam.serialize() returns JSON, not percent-encoded JSON. buildUrl concatenates the supplied strings and serialized parameters; it does not validate or escape them. Use a base URL without a query or fragment. The component overload adds / before a non-null path, so pass second/third, not /second/third. Percent-encode query keys and values when constructing externally delivered URLs, especially values containing &, +, #, or other URL delimiters. See type-safe parameters.

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuInit
import dev.theolm.rinku.treatAndFireDeepLink

fun ComponentActivity.RinkuInit(
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
)

fun Intent.treatAndFireDeepLink(
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
)

ComponentActivity is androidx.activity.ComponentActivity; Intent is android.content.Intent. Call RinkuInit once in onCreate. It handles the initial intent and listens for new intents, removing its listener on destruction. The intent extension processes dataString when present, applying filter then mapper. Exceptions from these steps propagate; final parsing uses asynchronous shared dispatch.

Alternatively, import dev.theolm.rinku.compose.ext.Rinku and call the activity extension:

@Composable
fun ComponentActivity.Rinku(
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
)

Use it inside the activity’s setContent, instead of RinkuInit. It owns the new-intent listener for the composition. Keep configuration stable: the listener is installed with DisposableEffect(Unit). The initial intent is processed in the composable body, so do not treat recomposition as a guaranteed one-time initialization boundary.

docs.title: iOS
docs.text:
Import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuIos in Kotlin, or the exported shared framework in Swift.

class RinkuIos(
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
) {
    fun onDeepLinkReceived(url: String)
    fun onDeepLinkReceived(userActivity: NSUserActivity)
}

NSUserActivity is platform.Foundation.NSUserActivity. Keep an adapter in your AppDelegate/SceneDelegate and forward the corresponding URL events. The activity overload accepts only NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb activities with a webpage URL. Both overloads filter, map, and use shared asynchronous dispatch. There is no start or close method. See iOS setup for framework export and Swift calls.

docs.title: JVM desktop
docs.text:
Import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuDesktop.

class RinkuDesktop(
    applicationId: String,
    schemes: Set<String>,
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
    onError: (Exception) -> Unit = { it.printStackTrace() },
) : AutoCloseable {
    enum class StartResult { PRIMARY, FORWARDED }
    fun start(args: Array<String> = emptyArray()): StartResult
    fun onDeepLinkReceived(url: String)
    override fun close()
}

Initialize before creating windows; keep the adapter alive until application shutdown. Use a stable, nonblank application ID and a nonempty set of valid schemes. Invalid constructor arguments throw IllegalArgumentException. start returns PRIMARY or FORWARDED; a forwarded process should return without opening a UI. Repeated starts return the original result. Closing is idempotent; starting after close throws IllegalStateException. Startup/IPC failures throw rather than opening a second instance.

Only syntactically valid absolute URIs matching configured schemes are accepted. Unsupported/invalid inputs and inputs over 16,384 UTF-16 code units are ignored; more than 64 accepted startup URLs throws IllegalArgumentException. Filtering, mapping, and queueing run on the receiving thread. Mapping, parsing, overflow, and incoming IPC errors go to onError; keep it non-throwing. Scheme registration and window focus are application responsibilities. See the desktop guide for IPC and packaging.

docs.title: Web
docs.text:
Import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuWeb.

class RinkuWeb(
    captureInitialUrl: Boolean = true,
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
    onError: (Exception) -> Unit = { it.printStackTrace() },
) {
    fun start()
    fun close()
}

Start before creating the UI and close on disposal. Only one adapter can be active per page. Repeated starts do nothing; closing is idempotent and leaves queued events intact. A closed adapter cannot restart. Starting after close or while another adapter owns the page throws IllegalStateException. Filter/mapper, parsing, and overflow errors go to onError; keep it non-throwing. Initialization/ownership errors throw to the caller.

The adapter receives the full initial URL (unless disabled) and subsequent popstate events. It does not intercept pushState/replaceState, observe hashchange, write history, or remove deployment prefixes. Hosting must provide an SPA fallback.

Alternatively, import dev.theolm.rinku.compose.ext.Rinku:

@Composable
fun Rinku(
    captureInitialUrl: Boolean = true,
    deepLinkFilter: DeepLinkFilter? = null,
    deepLinkMapper: DeepLinkMapper? = null,
    onError: (Exception) -> Unit = { it.printStackTrace() },
    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
)

The Web wrapper owns an adapter with DisposableEffect. Changing capture/filter/mapper configuration replaces it and can capture the current URL again; changing onError alone does not. Do not combine it with manual initialization. This is a Web-only top-level wrapper, not a shared wrapper for iOS or desktop. See the Web guide.

docs.title: Verified integration examples
docs.text:
Start with the setup guide for dependencies and native registration, then use the API reference for defaults, exceptions, and lifecycle rules. These examples track main, not necessarily the latest published Maven release.

The code blocks below are included directly from compiled/tested source files when MkDocs builds the site. They are not separately maintained copies. In the raw Markdown, follow the source links to read the complete code. Missing included files fail the documentation build.

docs.title: Shared parsing and serializable parameters
docs.text:
This complete test class demonstrates parsing a percent-encoded query, deserializing a model, building an internal URL, and handling a missing parameter. It requires the kotlinx.serialization compiler plugin and JSON dependency; assertions use kotlin.test. The sample’s simple JSON value is safe for internal dispatch; buildUrl does not percent-encode values for external delivery.

Test source

package dev.theolm.rinku

import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkParam
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertFailsWith

class DocumentationExamplesTest {
    @Serializable
    data class User(val name: String)

    @Test
    fun parseEncodedLink() {
        val link = DeepLink(
            "https://example.com/second/third?user=%7B%22name%22%3A%22Theo%22%7D"
        )

        assertEquals("https", link.schema)
        assertEquals("example.com", link.host)
        assertEquals(listOf("second", "third"), link.pathSegments)
        assertEquals(User("Theo"), link.getParameter("user", User.serializer()))
    }

    @Test
    fun buildInternalLink() {
        val parameter = DeepLinkParam("user", User("Theo"), User.serializer())
        val url = Rinku.buildUrl("https://example.com/second", parameter)

        assertEquals("{\"name\":\"Theo\"}", parameter.serialize())
        assertEquals(User("Theo"), DeepLink(url).getParameter("user", User.serializer()))
    }

    @Test
    fun buildLinkFromComponents() {
        val url = Rinku.buildUrl(schema = "https", host = "example.com", path = "second/third")

        assertEquals("https://example.com/second/third", url)
    }

    @Test
    fun rejectMissingParameter() {
        val link = DeepLink("https://example.com/second")

        assertFailsWith<IllegalArgumentException> {
            link.getParameter("user", User.serializer())
        }
    }
}

Run just these examples on JVM:

./gradlew :rinku-core:jvmTest --tests 'dev.theolm.rinku.DocumentationExamplesTest'

They also belong to the shared test suite run by the existing iOS and JS/Wasm CI jobs. No platform adapter or OS scheme registration is needed for these parsing tests.

docs.title: Shared Compose listener
docs.text:
The Voyager sample keeps a single DeepLinkListener in its shared root. Navigation is application-owned: toScreenStack() and screens.First belong to the sample, not Rinku. Use your own route interpretation if you do not use Voyager.

Shared UI source

import androidx.compose.material.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import cafe.adriel.voyager.navigator.CurrentScreen
import cafe.adriel.voyager.navigator.Navigator
import dev.theolm.rinku.DeepLink
import dev.theolm.rinku.compose.ext.DeepLinkListener
import screens.First

/**
 * Represents the root composable function of the application. It listens for deep link changes
 * and updates the UI accordingly by navigating to the relevant screen.
 * Depending on the deep link received, the application navigates to different screens within the app.
 */
@Composable
fun App() {
    // State holding the current deep link. Initially, there is no deep link (null).
    var deepLink by remember { mutableStateOf<DeepLink?>(null) }

    // Listens for deep link changes. When a deep link is received, the state is updated.
    DeepLinkListener {
        deepLink = it
    }

    // Renders the main screen of the application, passing the current deep link.
    MainScreen(deepLink)
}

/**
 * The main screen of the application. It decides which screen stack to display based on the
 * current deep link.
 *
 * @param deepLink The current deep link received by the application. It may be null, indicating
 * that no deep link is currently being handled.
 */
@Composable
private fun MainScreen(deepLink: DeepLink?) {
    // Calculates the screen stack to be displayed based on the deep link. This is recalculated
    // every time the deep link changes.
    val screenStack = remember(deepLink) {
        deepLink.toScreenStack()
    }

    MaterialTheme {
        // Initializes the navigator with the first screen. Depending on the current screen stack,
        // it may navigate to different screens within the app.
        Navigator(screen = First()) {
            CurrentScreen()
            // Replaces the entire screen stack based on the current deep link. This ensures that
            // the app navigates to the appropriate screen.
            remember(screenStack) {
                it.replaceAll(screenStack)
            }
        }
    }
}

For a non-Compose collector, use listenForDeepLinks in a lifecycle-owned coroutine scope; see common setup. Do not collect simultaneously through both APIs expecting a broadcast.

docs.title: iOS entry point
docs.text:
This is the sample’s AppDelegate-based entry point, not a SwiftUI @main lifecycle. ComposeApp is the exported shared framework; ContentView is the sample’s SwiftUI host. Forward URL events from your SceneDelegate instead if your application uses scenes, including its initial connection events.

Swift source

import SwiftUI
import ComposeApp

@UIApplicationMain
class AppDelegate: NSObject, UIApplicationDelegate {
    var window: UIWindow?
    let rinku = RinkuIos.init(deepLinkFilter: nil, deepLinkMapper: nil)

    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey : Any]? = nil) -> Bool {
        self.window = UIWindow(frame: UIScreen.main.bounds)
        let mainViewController = UIHostingController(rootView: ContentView())
        self.window!.rootViewController = mainViewController
        self.window!.makeKeyAndVisible()

        return true
    }

    func application(_ app: UIApplication, open url: URL, options: [UIApplication.OpenURLOptionsKey : Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
        rinku.onDeepLinkReceived(url: url.absoluteString)
        return true
    }

    func application(_ application: UIApplication, continue userActivity: NSUserActivity, restorationHandler: @escaping ([UIUserActivityRestoring]?) -> Void) -> Bool {
        rinku.onDeepLinkReceived(userActivity: userActivity)
        return true
    }
}

Open samples/voyager/iosApp/iosApp.xcodeproj on macOS and run the iosApp scheme on an Apple Silicon simulator or device. The existing CI tests the Kotlin iOS adapter and compiles the Compose extension, but does not build this Swift application. Verify Swift integration and cold/warm native URL delivery in Xcode before shipping.

docs.title: JVM desktop entry point
docs.text:
Initialize before creating windows, return immediately when forwarding to a primary instance, and close the adapter after the UI exits. App is the shared root above.

Desktop source

import androidx.compose.ui.window.Window
import androidx.compose.ui.window.application
import dev.theolm.rinku.RinkuDesktop

fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    RinkuDesktop(
        applicationId = "dev.theolm.rinku.sample.voyager",
        schemes = setOf("rinku-voyager"),
    ).use { rinku ->
        if (rinku.start(args) == RinkuDesktop.StartResult.FORWARDED) return
        application(exitProcessOnExit = false) {
            Window(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "Rinku — Voyager") {
                App()
            }
        }
    }
}

./gradlew :samples:voyager:desktopApp:run --args='rinku-voyager://example/second/third'

Desktop CI compiles this sample on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Running through Gradle does not register a native URL scheme; see packaging and OS verification.

docs.title: Web entry point and adapter ownership
docs.text:
The entry point creates the browser UI. WebDemo owns the Rinku adapter and implements application-controlled history buttons. Do not add another adapter around it.

Web entry source

import androidx.compose.ui.ExperimentalComposeUiApi
import androidx.compose.ui.window.ComposeViewport
import dev.theolm.rinku.common.WebDemo
import kotlinx.browser.document

@OptIn(ExperimentalComposeUiApi::class)
fun main() {
    ComposeViewport(document.getElementById("app")!!) {
        WebDemo { App() }
    }
}

Web adapter and history source

package dev.theolm.rinku.common

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.material.Button
import androidx.compose.material.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import dev.theolm.rinku.Rinku
import dev.theolm.rinku.compose.ext.Rinku as RinkuHost
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkFilter
import dev.theolm.rinku.models.DeepLinkMapper
import kotlinx.browser.document
import kotlinx.browser.window

/** History writes belong to this sample application, never to the Rinku adapter. */
@Composable
fun WebDemo(content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    val origin = window.location.origin
    // Set this meta tag when deploying under a prefix, for example /rinku/.
    val basePath = remember {
        document.querySelector("meta[name='rinku-base-path']")?.getAttribute("content") ?: "/"
    }
    val filter = remember(origin) {
        object : DeepLinkFilter {
            override fun isValid(url: String) = url.startsWith("$origin/")
        }
    }
    val mapper = remember(origin, basePath) {
        object : DeepLinkMapper {
            override fun map(url: String) = if (url.startsWith("$origin$basePath")) {
                "$origin/" + url.removePrefix("$origin$basePath")
            } else {
                url
            }
        }
    }
    RinkuHost(deepLinkFilter = filter, deepLinkMapper = mapper) {
        Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
            Text("History is controlled by the sample; Rinku receives initial URLs and Back/Forward.")
            Row {
                Button(onClick = { window.history.back() }) { Text("Browser back") }
                Button(onClick = { window.history.forward() }) { Text("Browser forward") }
            }
            Row {
                listOf("", "second", "second/third").forEach { route ->
                    Button(onClick = {
                        window.history.pushState(null, "", "$basePath$route?source=web")
                        // pushState does not fire popstate. Notify shared navigation explicitly,
                        // applying the same filter/mapper as the browser adapter, exactly once.
                        Rinku.handleDeepLink(window.location.href, applyFilter = true, applyMapper = true)
                    }) { Text(route.ifEmpty { "Home" }) }
                }
            }
            Column(Modifier.weight(1f)) { content() }
        }
    }
}

Run one target at a time:

./gradlew :samples:voyager:webApp:jsBrowserDevelopmentRun
./gradlew :samples:voyager:webApp:wasmJsBrowserDevelopmentRun

Web CI bundles both targets and runs shared, browser-history, and Compose lifecycle tests. Direct navigation/reload also requires an SPA fallback from your production host. See Web hosting and deployment prefixes.
